The interiors are as aesthetic as other Subko cafés, but the atmosphere here feels a bit different. With its double-height ceiling, the space feels cozy yet airy and fresh at the same time, which makes it very pleasant to sit and relax.

The staff was good and welcoming. As expected, the coffee, desserts, and baked items are consistent with other Subko outlets — always amazing and delicious, no complaints there. Their coffee is still among the best you can have.

The food menu, however, was a bit underwhelming for me personally. The options are quite limited compared to the Mary Lodge outlet, and honestly, I’ve never found Subko’s food bowls or sandwiches to be particularly tasty. This could just be personal taste, but the food didn’t really stand out.

That said, there’s no doubt the place itself is superb. It’s great to visit with friends, for a casual date, or even solo if you just want to enjoy one of the best coffees around. For coffee, desserts, ambience, and a good time — it won’t disappoint.

featured_reviews.name: Siddhesh Vichare
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐ 1/5 (Only because 0 stars isn’t an option)

Absolutely one of the worst breakfast experiences I’ve ever had.

We ordered two Kuckeliku Breakfast Platters — one with Pancakes & Yogurt Bowl and another with French Toast & Chia Seed Bowl. From the moment the food arrived, something felt seriously off.

The yogurt and chia bowls both had a strange smell and unpleasant taste. The sausages smelled stale, as if they had been sitting out for hours. The potatoes tasted and smelled like they had been cooked days ago and repeatedly reheated before being served.

The French toast looked completely unappetizing and honestly appeared unfit to eat. We didn’t even attempt to touch it. The pancakes were rubbery, dense, and served with what looked like a watery, glue-like syrup rather than anything resembling fresh pancake syrup.

For beverages, we ordered one hot latte and one cold latte. The hot latte was passable, but the cold latte looked like coffee-coloured water with almost no body, texture, or flavour.

The fried eggs were average at best, but the omelette was genuinely awful — soggy, wet, undercooked, and leaking liquid when cut into. It was difficult to believe it had passed any quality check before being served.

What was most alarming was the smell. Freshly prepared food usually has a pleasant aroma the moment it reaches the table. These platters did the exact opposite. The unpleasant smell was immediately noticeable and made the entire experience uncomfortable.

We informed the manager about the condition of the food, left almost everything untouched, paid the bill, and walked out.

What makes this experience even more disappointing is the amount we spent. We paid for a breakfast that was largely inedible. Leaving expensive food untouched because it simply wasn’t fit to eat is frustrating and feels like a complete waste of money.

I’ve attached photos so others can judge for themselves. Based on this experience, I would not recommend this place to anyone.

Bono icecream used to be genuinely good when it started. The quality has fallen and how. I tried a "Bono bar" and I'm really questioning the ingredients listed on the package. After about 2 bites I had to throw the bar into the trash, it was that bad.

They claim they use Belgian chocolate in the ice cream and the shell. I would be interested to know what Belgian chocolate they are using, the shell tastes like they use cheap chocolate compound. How does this fancy boutique icecream taste WORSE than a Magnum bar?! Someone should do a lab test and verify their "honest ingredients" claim...

featured_reviews.review_text:
Cafe Churchill is one of those charming little places that proves great food doesn't need a fancy setting. Nestled in the heart of Colaba Causeway, this small, Parsi-run café has a warm, old-world charm and serves delicious, comforting food. Everything we ordered was excellent, but the standouts were definitely the Beef Teriyaki, Butter Garlic Beef Steak, and the Mixed Grill Lasagna. Each dish was packed with flavour, cooked perfectly, and served in generous portions. The food tasted fresh, hearty, and made with care. If you're looking for a cozy spot with authentic character, friendly service, and consistently good food, Cafe Churchill is well worth a visit. A true Colaba classic that keeps you wanting to come back for more!
PS: there is no parking available during peak hours.

featured_reviews.name: Sagar Tipnis
featured_reviews.review_text:

Tried their King Solomon Steak, but it was too well-done for my liking rendering it chewy - would've preferred it medium or medium-rare. The fish dish was quite good; overall do visit if you are a fan of non-Indian, non-Asian fare, and want a large no. of options to choose from.

Absolutely no parking available anywhere, so do use public transport (BEST Colaba Bus Depot / Electric House bus stop is just next to this restaurant) or cabs!

featured_reviews.name: D M
featured_reviews.review_text:
If I were to rate the cafe's concept, it would be a 5! But if you ask me about my overall experience, it will be strictly a 3.

The ambience is bang on perfect for hanging out with friends. There are books stacked like a mini library which you can read while you enjoy a bite. The food that we tried was so not great though. We tried:

•White sauce chicken pasta
•Chicken B2BLC sandwich
•Cold coffee with almond milk (of which the almond milk quantity was only available for 1 serve. Disappointing.)
•Cold coffee with hazelnut
•Paneer pesto crepe
•Chicken fingers

Overall, the pasta was the winner. It was cooked very well with the sauce tasting creamy and delicious. It was served with the normal bread cut into triangles and toasted. The sandwich size was quite huge with a good amount of filling. Not at all a fan of both the cold coffees - One with almond milk and the other with cow milk. The paneer pesto wrap didn’t have salt and the taste was quite off and not balanced. It’s supposed to be creamy but instead we could taste only the greens. It was a total letdown. The crepe covering was nice though but again what’s the point? Chicken fingers seemed a bit over-fried and stale served with a sauce (it was definitely not mayonnaise as told to us) which did not go well. We chose not to eat all 6 pieces as a result.

The service was alright. The server made a face when we could not finish everything on the plate and commented that it would be given to someone else. Now I understand that’s very noble of them to do that to prevent food wastage. I politely replied on the same lines with a smile. His tone seemed rude nor were there any other mannerisms leaving us baffled and uncomfortable.

Overall not a great experience and would skip returning.

featured_reviews.name: Avi Kadu
featured_reviews.review_text:
First of all, gratitude to the owner for working towards the development of the society. I have also read your personal journey, and it is truly inspiring to see where you started and what you have built today.
However, I would like to share my honest feedback about the food quality and service, which was disappointing during our visit.
I ordered a coffee, but it was not hot. I finished it quietly without creating any issue; you may even check the CCTV if required. However, proper serving temperature should be ensured.
We ordered a chicken omelette with cheese, but honestly, it was difficult to find the chicken in it. Initially, I thought there might be chunks inside, but there were no visible shreds or proper quantity. That was quite disappointing.
We also ordered nachni pancakes, and the dish was served with cold caramel sauce that seemed straight from the fridge.
Ideally, the server should inform whether the sauce will be served on the side or on top. Warm pancakes with apple and caramel sauce should not be cold, as it completely spoils the taste of the dish.
When the bill came, the lady at the counter suggested we need not pay due to the experience. However, we respect your effort and the noble work you are doing, so we chose to pay.
Sir, basic training for the chef and kitchen team is necessary. My child is autistic, and after waiting patiently for quite some time, receiving such food was disappointing for us. Eventually, we left the place dissatisfied.
I must mention that the server was good and well-trained, but he was slightly pushy while promoting initiatives. Sometimes this can irritate guests, so a balanced approach would help.
Please understand that we are genuine food lovers and not here to damage anyone’s reputation. We appreciate your noble work and truly hope you continue doing it. Just focus a little more on food quality, serving standards, and taste, and the place can become even better.
✅ Suggested Next Step:
If you want, I can also create a shorter, sharper Google review (more impactful and slightly aggressive) which usually gets faster attention from restaurant management.

featured_reviews.name: Stephen Antu Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely loved this place! The ambience is calm, welcoming, and has a beautiful vibe that instantly makes you feel at ease. I tried the Pink Sauce Pasta and the Spanish Omelette—the food was really good and well-prepared.

The service was handled by Jyoti (I hope I’ve got the name right—referring to the tall girl who also models), and she was excellent throughout. There was a small glitch in service because of which we couldn’t fully enjoy the Spanish Omelette, but Kushboo handled the feedback very gracefully. The way she spoke about the café’s story and its origin was truly inspiring.

It’s not just a café—it’s a place with a heart. Definitely worth visiting, especially to hear the story from Kushboo herself.

I’m giving one star less only because there’s room for improvement in the service, which I’m sure can be fixed with a little bit of training.
